name: uvw
reason: README (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) and repo tree (docs, src, test, subprojects; no bench directory) hold no benchmark, no number and no comparison with libuv, libevent or Asio. It only says 'tiny and easy to use' and that it stays true to libuv's API. The issue search for benchmark, performance or overhead returned no issue with such a title or figures. A web search found no published uvw overhead measurement. Nothing to report.

name: WAMP
listed_description: Provides RPC and pub/sub messaging patterns.
reason: WAMP is a protocol specification, not a code library: the wamp-proto repo README carries no performance text, and the Crossbar.io router README (crossbario/crossbar, the main reference router, opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) has no benchmark, throughput or latency numbers. wamp.ws and wamp-proto.org were not reachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). A web search found no published Crossbar.io or WAMP throughput comparison against another RPC or pub/sub framework; the only numbers it surfaced (4.57M msgs/s) belong to an unrelated .NET library. No numeric comparison against a baseline.

name: Wangle
listed_description: A client/server application framework to build asynchronous, event-driven modern C++ services.
reason: README has one performance sentence, for OutputBufferingHandler: 'it can improve throughput for small writes by up to 300%'. The comparison is buffered versus unbuffered writes inside Wangle's own pipeline, with no named external baseline, no benchmark code, compiler, flags or hardware. The repo tree (acceptor, bootstrap, channel, client, codec, example, service, ssl, test, util) has no bench or perf directory. A web search for Wangle benchmarks against Netty, Boost.Asio or proxygen found none. No numeric comparison against a recognizable baseline.

name: WebSocket++
listed_description: C++/Boost Asio based websocket client/server library.
reason: readme.md, changelog.md, docs/faq.dox and docs/manual.dox (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) give only directional claims ('high performance' as a goal; changelog 'numerous performance improvements' with no numbers). The repo has no benchmark directory. Numbers that mention it come from other projects' pages and show it as the slower side: the uWebSockets README table (search snippet only, not opened; self-reported, WebSocket++ v0.7.0, about 3x slower on short messages) and a Habr localhost echo test (page unreachable here, search snippets conflicting; websocketpp p50 comparable and p99 not better than Boost.Beast). No number shows WebSocket++ beating a named baseline.

name: Wslay
listed_description: WebSocket library. Implements version 13 of the WebSocket protocol (RFC 6455).
reason: README.rst (opened via raw.githubusercontent.com) only links Autobahn conformance reports, which measure protocol correctness, not speed; the ChangeLog is empty, NEWS has no performance text, and the issue search for benchmark, performance or faster found nothing relevant. The project site (tatsuhiro-t.github.io) is blocked here. A web search found no benchmark that includes wslay. No numeric comparison against any baseline.
